title: Reliability governance operational timetable (90d)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working 90-day operational timetable to align reliability governance across serving runtime, platform-engineering, observability, product (hosted API & Dedicated), and customer-success. Goal: reduce incident mean time to resolution (MTTR) for model-serving degradations by 40% and increase SLO adoption coverage to 85% of customer-facing routes.

Scope & constraints:
- Focused on model-serving SLOs (latency, availability, and inference correctness signals) for hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Does not replace per-service runbooks; this is the governance cadence and handoff schedule.
- We will iterate weekly; artifacts produced become canonical on Confluence INF-480 once approved.

High-level objectives (measurable):
1) SLO coverage: Identify and onboard SLOs for 25 priority routes (target by day 45).
2) Error budget policy: Define unified error-budget enforcement (automatic throttles + routing fallback) within 60 days.
3) Observability: Standardized dashboards and alert templates for SLOs (p95/p99 latency, success-rate) across hosted/dedicated by day 30.
4) Cross-team readiness: Training + game-day drills with CS and Solutions by day 75.

Key roles (single-line responsibilities):
- Reliability Steward: Aisha Kapoor — governance owner, weekly cadence chair, final approver for threshold changes.
- SLO Author (team level): Feature teams (product-hosted-api, dedicated) — draft SLOs and acceptance criteria.
- Runtime Partner: Marcus Lee (serving-runtime) — feasibility & mitigation design for latency/throughput SLOs.
- Observability Owner: Elena García — dashboard/alert templates, tracing hooks.
- Ops Escalation Lead: Tom Reynolds (SRE) — incident handling protocol and triage corridor owner.
- Customer Impact Lead: Priya Nair (customer-success) — quantifies customer-level impact and comms playbook.

90-day phased timetable (weeks):
Phase 0: Prep (week 0, days 0–7)
- Kickoff sync: governance charter + OKRs, invite list, tooling checklist (PagerDuty, Datadog, Alertmanager). Owner: Aisha.
- Inventory: quick audit of current SLOs, dashboards, and routes (extract from model-serving catalog). Owner: Elena + Feature teams.

Phase 1: Define & Baseline (weeks 1–4, days 8–30)
Week 1 (8–14):
- Workshop: SLO definition lab (product + runtime + obs). Output: SLO template per route (service, metric, objective, window, burn-rate). Owner: Aisha + Marcus.
- Baseline measurements: collect 90-day historical latency/availability percentiles. Owner: Elena.
Week 2 (15–21):
- Risk catalog: list top 10 failure modes that could violate SLOs (e.g., KV cache eviction spikes, quantized kernel regressions, model OOM). Owner: Marcus + Tom.
- Draft alert thresholds and alert routing map. Owner: Elena.
Week 3–4 (22–30):
- Team review cycles: feature teams propose SLOs for 25 priority routes. Each proposal includes runbook stub and rollback criteria. Owner: Feature teams.
- Decision board meeting: accept/reject SLOs, record exceptions. Owner: Reliability Steward.

Phase 2: Implement & Integrate (weeks 5–9, days 31–60)
Week 5–6 (31–44):
- Observability implementation: standardized dashboards, SLO objects in monitoring (slo:namespace:route). Owner: Elena.
- Alerting automation: connect SLO burn-rate alerts to PagerDuty escalation policies and Slack channels. Owner: Elena + SRE.
Week 7 (45–51):
- Error budget policy draft: define automated enforcements (rate-limit, fallback to cheaper model variant, region failover) and manual governance steps. Owner: Aisha + Product.
- Onboarding target: achieve 25 SLOs onboarded (target day 45).
Week 8–9 (52–60):
- Canary drills: run simulated degradations with controlled error budget burns. Measure MTTR and alert fidelity. Owner: Tom + Marcus.
- Adjust thresholds and runbook steps based on drill findings.

Phase 3: Harden & Handoff (weeks 10–13, days 61–90)
Week 10 (61–67):
- Policy finalization: publish error budget enforcement playbook and decision matrix. Owner: Aisha.
- Training: 1-hour training sessions for CS & Solutions engineered to respond to SLO alerts. Owner: Priya + Tom.
Week 11–12 (68–83):
- Game days: two full-scope game days covering cross-region failure, model-serving throughput saturation, and cache-consistency loss. Capture playbook gaps.
- Post-mortem templating: create standard SLO incident postmortem template linking to SLO change requests.
Week 13 (84–90):
- Handoff: transition stewardship to rotating SLO on-call roster and schedule recurring monthly governance review.
- Metrics review: measured against objectives; produce executive summary and recommended next steps.

Decision gates (explicit criteria):
- Gate A (Day 30): >=80% of priority routes have baseline data and candidate SLOs. If not met, freeze onboarding and run focused measurement sprint.
- Gate B (Day 60): Observability + alerting wired and 1–2 canary drills executed with median MTTR improvement. If not met, delay error-budget enforcement.
- Gate C (Day 90): 85% SLO coverage for priority routes + training done. If not met, extend 30-day stabilization.

Communication & meeting cadence:
- Weekly governance sync (30 min) — owner: Aisha. Quick status, blockers, escalations.
- Bi-weekly technical deep-dive (60 min) — rotating owner (Marcus/Elena). Dive on failures and mitigation changes.
- Game-day debriefs within 48 hours; summary to execs within 5 business days.
- SLO change proposals: via GitHub PR style workflow in repo observability/slo-defs with linked Jira tickets.

Tooling & templates to deliver:
- SLO template (Confluence + YAML sample for monitoring ingestion).
- Alert templates (burn-rate, latency increase, success-rate drop).
- Runbook stubs per route with quick rollback actions and fallback models.
- On-call escalation matrix and PagerDuty policies.

Risk matrix (top items + mitigations):
- Risk: Overly aggressive latency SLOs cause flapping alerts. Mitigation: use rolling windows and multi-tier alerting (warning vs critical).
- Risk: Incorrectly scoped SLOs miss customer impact. Mitigation: include customer-success in definition and correlate with user-facing metrics.
- Risk: Tooling gaps (missing traces). Mitigation: mandatory tracing hooks for new routes and retrofitted instrumentation plan.

Next artifacts to produce (action items):
1) SLO definition lab notes and blank templates (due day 14) — owner: Aisha + Elena.
2) Inventory CSV of routes + historical percentiles (due day 21) — owner: Feature teams.
3) Draft error-budget enforcement policy doc (due day 45) — owner: Product + Aisha.
4) Game-day schedule and scenario list (due day 55) — owner: Tom.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Should internal-only administrative routes (billing reconciliation) carry full SLOs or a lightweight operational target? (proposal: lightweight).
- Do we auto-throttle per-customer on error budget breaches (privacy/UX considerations)? Need CS/legal input.

Appendix (short refs):
- Example SLOs (suggested for LLM-serving):
  * Latency: p95 < 250ms for small-text-generation routes (30s window), objective 99.5%
  * Availability: successful-response-rate >= 99.9% (24h window) for auth-dependent endpoints
  * Correctness proxy: rerank/call-fallback success-rate > 99% across A/B eval prompts
- Example enforcement options: slow-paths (queue + degrade response), fallback to quantized model, region failover, temporary quota reduction.

If you want I can: populate the inventory CSV template with the 25 priority routes (I can extract names from the model-serving catalog) and generate the Confluence-ready SLO YAML samples for the monitoring team.

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally operational and prescriptive; call out any governance conflicts or missing owners and tag in the Confluence thread linked above.
